recipes.title: Potato Leek Soup with Charred Leek Oil

items: ½ cup of unsalted butter (1 stick)

method.heading: Soup
steps: Separate the green and white parts of the leek and clean them separately (thoroughly, leeks are super dirty) before chopping the whites, reserve the greens to make the leek oil. Peel and cut potatoes into largeish cubes, keep potatoes in a bowl of cold water to rinse off excess starch until ready to use. Slice garlic, and if you have butcher’s twine, tie your thyme and bay leaf together.

Add butter to a large pot and melt over medium heat, add the white parts of the leek and sweat down (don’t want any browning) with a generous pinch of salt for 25-30 minutes until very soft. Add garlic, thyme, and bay leaf, and saute for another 5 minutes. Add potatoes and chicken stock, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered until the potatoes are almost falling apart, 30-35 minutes depending on how large you cut your potatoes. Remove thyme and bay leaf.

Blend in batches, making sure each batch has plenty of liquid, add a splash of cream to each batch to ensure it blends smoothly. Once everything is super smooth, strain the soup. Adjust consistency with additional stock or heavy cream to your desired texture. If you would like to melt in cheese, do it now (something like gruyere would be good). Finally, season to taste with salt and white pepper. Garnish with Leek Oil.

method.heading: Charred Leek Oil
steps: Pat dry washed leek greens before arranging about 1-2 cups of greens on a baking sheet lined with aluminum foil, drizzle with just a bit of a high smoke point oil such as vegetable oil.

Place under the broil on the upper rack of your oven, checking about every 45 seconds and turning to make sure it is getting evenly charred. Once lightly charred (but not burnt) on all sides, remove from the oven, this should take no more than 5 minutes.
Put charred leek greens in a blender and cover with vegetable oil, blend on high until smooth.

Add blended leek oil to a saucepan and cook over medium heat until it reaches 165 F. If you don’t have a thermometer, it is ready when you can see bubbles rising around the edges of the saucepan. Strain through a cheesecloth lined sieve.
Use to garnish the soup or whatever else you’d like, store by freezing for up to 6 months.

recipes.title: Roasted Carrots with Harissa and Smoked Paprika Brown Butter

items: ½ tsp Harissa paste (more or less as desired)
A few roasted hazelnuts, chopped roughly

method.heading: Carrots
steps: Preheat oven to 400°
Toss carrots with a generous glug of olive oil, salt, pepper, cumin, powdered ginger, and ½ tbsp of smoked paprika
Arrange carrots on a lined baking sheet with a few smashed garlic cloves
Roast for roughly 25 minutes, turning halfway through. Check doneness by piercing the thickest carrot with a knife, it should go in and out with next to no resistance.

method.heading: Yogurt
steps: Mix yogurt with a pinch of salt, grated garlic, lemon juice, and lemon zest
Allow to come to room temperature before plating

method.heading: Brown Butter
steps: Heat butter over low heat until nicely browned, careful not to let it burn. Should take 5-7 minutes to get to this point.
Mix in harissa and stir vigorously until fully incorporated.
Take off heat and add remaining smoked paprika, stir until incorporated.

method.heading: Plating
steps: Spread yogurt on the bottom of a wide bowl or plate
Place carrots as well as protein (if using) on top of yogurt.
Spoon over brown butter and then sprinkle hazelnuts on top. (chopped parsley could be a nice touch too)

recipes.title: Sautéed Radish with Sage and Brown Butter

items: 2 cups chopped Radish, cleaned and stems removed

steps: Heat 1 tbsp of butter in a medium sauté pan until foamy, add radish and season with a generous pinch of salt, pepper, and roughly a half tsp of ground cloves
Cook over medium heat for roughly 35 minutes until nicely browned and soft
After 10 minutes, add sugar, after another 15 add whole sage leaves
Continue cooking deglazing with wine or water as needed
Meanwhile, heat two remaining tbsp of butter over medium low heat until browned.
Once fully cooked, remove sage and adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve with brown butter spooned on top as a side dish to any hearty main.
Wash and dry Swiss Chard
Trim leaves from stems, discard stems.
Roughly chop leaves
Thinly slice garlic
Preheat dry pan until hot (~3 min over medium-low heat)
Add olive oil to the pan and wait a few seconds before adding chopped leaves.
Cook over medium high for ~1 min until it starts to wilt.
Add sliced garlic and continue cooking until fragrant, ~30 seconds.
Add a splash of lemon juice and continue cooking until completely absorbed/evaporated.
Take off heat and serve, goes well on sandwiches or as a side to many proteins (Steak works well as well as chicken).

items: ¼ cup grated parm + more for serving

steps: Cook pasta according to package instructions (or however you like it cooked)
While pasta is cooking, cut garlic clove in half and rub the cut side around the inside of a large mixing bowl
Add lemon juice to mixing bowl followed by olive oil, mix vigorously until emulsified.
Add parm and mix until a paste forms, add salt and pepper.
Add cooked pasta along with a splash of hot pasta water to mixing bowl and toss vigorously for a couple minutes until a smooth glossy sauce forms
Add fresh basil leaves to bowl and continue tossing for another minute
Serve topped with more grated parm and a drizzle of olive oil.
